title: 모음 ㅓ·ㅗ·ㅜ 연습
unresolved: Exercise 5 ('In the minimal set 서 / 소 / 수, which syllable has ㅜ?') repeats exercises 1 and 3. Exercise 1 already asked about 서, and exercise 3 already had the learner compare 소/수 and answer '수 (ㅜ)'. So exercise 5 only repeats a question already answered, with the same syllables, and makes the worksheet thinner. Replace it with an item that uses new words, e.g. 'Pick the word whose first syllable has ㅜ: 거울 / 두부 / 오리' (answer: 두부), or have the learner write the vowel in each syllable of a new word such as 두부 or 머리.

review: Exercise 3 (answer 3): The word '우유' has two vowels: ㅜ in '우' and ㅠ in '유'. The question 'Which vowel appears in the word '우유'?' does not limit the choices, so ㅠ is also a correct answer, but 'ㅜ' is the only answer given. Fix: ask about the first syllable, e.g. 'Which vowel is in the first syllable of '우유'? (Write ㅓ, ㅗ, or ㅜ)'. Or use a word that only has ㅜ, e.g. '구두' (shoes) or '두부' (tofu). The same issue affects exercise 4: '엄마' and '수박' also contain ㅏ, and '오이' also contains ㅣ. Add '(choose from ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ)' to exercise 4 so there is only one correct answer.
audit: exercises[2] (3번): Which vowel appears in the word '우유'? → Which of ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅜ appears in the word '우유'?

exercises[3] (4번): Match these words to the vowel they contain (write three symbols in order): 엄마 / 오이 / 수박 → Match these words to the vowel (ㅓ, ㅗ, or ㅜ) they contain (write three symbols in order): 엄마 / 오이 / 수박

review: The objective says learners will 'recognize and correctly pronounce' ㅓ, ㅗ and ㅜ, but all six exercises (1–6) are written recognition tasks (write down the vowel symbol). None of them practises pronunciation. Add one or two pronunciation items, e.g. 'Read aloud: 서 / 소 / 수 — listen for the difference between ㅓ and ㅗ' or 'Which vowel do you round your lips for, ㅓ or ㅗ?'. Otherwise, change the objective to recognition only.

Three of the nine example sentences use the same 'X을/를 먹어요' frame (먹다: 밥을 먹어요, 오이: 오이를 먹어요, 수박: 수박을 먹어요). This makes the sheet thin. Change at least two of them to different frames, e.g. 수박: '수박이 커요.' (The watermelon is big.) and 오이: '오이가 맛있어요.' (The cucumber is tasty.).

The exercises also repeat the same pattern. Exercises 1, 2 and 3 all ask which vowel is in a single word, and exercises 4 and 6 are the same three-word matching task. Replace some of them with different task types, such as reading the ㅓ/ㅗ minimal pair 거기/고기 aloud or sorting the words by vowel.

Exercises 2 and 3 repeat the same task. Both ask only which vowel, ㅓ or ㅗ, rounds the lips: exercise 2 with 거기 / 고기, exercise 3 with the bare vowels. Nothing in the worksheet practises telling ㅗ and ㅜ apart by sound; exercise 5 only asks the learner to spot ㅜ in writing. That leaves a gap in the goal of pronouncing all three vowels correctly. Replace exercise 3 with a ㅗ-vs-ㅜ pronunciation task, for example: "Read aloud: 소 / 수. Both vowels round the lips. For which one is your mouth more closed and your lips pushed further forward?" The answer is 수 (ㅜ). Update answer 3 to match.

Exercise 5 ('In the minimal set 서 / 소 / 수, which syllable has ㅜ?') repeats exercises 1 and 3. Exercise 1 already asked about 서, and exercise 3 already had the learner compare 소/수 and answer '수 (ㅜ)'. So exercise 5 only repeats a question already answered, with the same syllables, and makes the worksheet thinner. Replace it with an item that uses new words, e.g. 'Pick the word whose first syllable has ㅜ: 거울 / 두부 / 오리' (answer: 두부), or have the learner write the vowel in each syllable of a new word such as 두부 or 머리.

fixes.problem: 'eo' is the romanization of ㅓ and was replaced by 'é', a front vowel, which is misleading. Also, 'vogal aberta e mediana' is not the standard phonetic term for an open-mid vowel.
The 'ó' in 'só' is a rounded vowel, but ㅓ (like the 'u' in English 'cup') is unrounded. This contradicts line 29, which asks the learner which word rounds the lips.
fixes.fix: como o 'ó' de 'só', mas sem arredondar os lábios (aproximado)

fixes.problem: 「韓語」 is not the normal Japanese word for the Korean language; the standard term is 「韓国語」.
fixes.fix: 韓国語の母音ㅓ、ㅗ、ㅜを認識して発音する練習。各母音につき簡単な単語を3つと短い例文を示します。

fixes.problem: The romanization 'eo' (for ㅓ) was changed to « eu ». In standard romanization, 'eu' stands for a different vowel (ㅡ), so learners could confuse ㅓ with ㅡ. The romanization should stay 'eo'.
